claims.text: Conventional casting of CoCrFeNiTi produces a porous, homogeneous but soft single-phase material with hardness below 200 HV.
High-energy ball milling at 400 rpm for 4 hours with cooling intervals is an applicable precursor treatment for the proposed alloy.
SPS at 1050 °C and 30 MPa, using 50 °C/min from 600–900 °C and 25 °C/min from 900–1050 °C with a 5-minute dwell, is the proposed rapid-sintering regime.
Rapid SPS under this regime will reduce residual porosity below 1%.
The proposed treatment will produce an FCC-dominated solid solution containing less than 10% BCC phase.
The proposed treatment will produce grains smaller than 500 nm.
High heating rates and a short dwell kinetically suppress diffusion-controlled HCP formation in CoCrFeNiTi.
The processing route suppresses Ti-rich or Nb/Ti-rich Laves phases.
A high density of grain boundaries and solute drag from Ti/Nb segregation prevent HCP nucleation.
Severe plastic deformation during milling contributes to suppression of diffusion-controlled HCP and Laves transformations.
High strain rate and applied pressure during SPS eliminate porosity.
Rapid thermal expansion and contraction during sintering constitute a high strain-rate condition favorable to dual-phase stability.
The processed alloy will have Vickers hardness above 300 HV and significantly above the cast-state hardness.
The processed alloy will retain greater ductility than brittle HCP-dominant alloys.
Temperatures above 1100 °C or dwell times above 15 minutes permit enough diffusion for HCP or Laves-phase formation.
Adding 0.5 at.% carbon can stabilize a single FCC phase in related Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo alloys that otherwise exhibit FCC plus HCP.
A Vickers indentation test at 500 g load with a 15-second dwell is proposed.
A slower 25 °C/min heating rate combined with a 30-minute dwell will induce HCP formation in the control sample.
More than 15% HCP or hardness below 250 HV in the rapid-sintered sample would falsify the processing hypothesis.
A hardness increase that occurs without grain refinement but correlates with solute clustering would falsify grain refinement as the strengthening mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes SPS at 1050 °C with a heating rate of 50 °C/min, whereas the detailed intervention specifies only 25 °C/min over the final 900–1050 °C interval.
The stated alloy is CoCrFeNiTi and contains no Nb, yet the mediator and mechanism invoke Nb segregation and Nb/Ti-rich Laves phases as if Nb were present.
